answer: Time-locked fidelity bonds curb Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock collateral in an escrow contract before gaining marketplace access, with slashing on cryptographic fault proofs. An attacker incurs frozen liquidity and opportunity cost per identity, whether deploying agents to survey juniper stands, measure zenith irradiance, or track sable migrations.
